related_questions.question: What is the most common cause of lung nodules?

text_blocks.snippet: The most common cause of lung nodules is inflamed tissue from past infections or inflammation (granulomas). These are often benign and don't pose a significant health risk. Other common causes include benign lung tumors like hamartomas. While less frequent, lung cancer and other cancers that have spread to the lungs (metastatic cancer) can also cause lung nodules.
snippet_highlighted_words: inflamed tissue from past infections or inflammation (granulomas)

list.title: Infections:
list.snippet: When the body fights off an infection, it can sometimes leave behind small, scar-like areas in the lung called granulomas. These granulomas are a common cause of lung nodules and are usually benign.

list.title: Inflammation:
list.snippet: Conditions like sarcoidosis or rheumatoid arthritis can also cause inflammation in the lungs, leading to granuloma formation and subsequent lung nodules.

list.title: Benign Tumors:
list.snippet: Some benign tumors, such as hamartomas, can also appear as lung nodules.

list.title: Malignant (Cancerous) Tumors:
list.snippet: While less common, lung nodules can be the first sign of lung cancer, or they can be a result of cancer that has spread from another part of the body to the lungs.

list.title: Other Causes:
list.snippet: Less common causes include cysts, prior trauma, and even certain autoimmune diseases.
Most lung nodules are not cancerous.
If a nodule is found, it's important to get it evaluated by a doctor to determine the cause and whether further monitoring or treatment is needed.
Factors like smoking history, age, and family history can increase the risk of a lung nodule being cancerous.
